topic: Connectors and cables: identifying, testing and replacing them
title: Identify the connectors
instructions:
## What plugs in where?

A technician has to name a connector at a glance. Match each connector to what it carries or connects. Some options are distractors.

items.name: USB-C
items.answer: Reversible USB data, power and video

items.name: HDMI
items.answer: Digital video and audio to a monitor or TV

items.name: SATA data (7-pin, L-shaped)
items.answer: Hard disk or 2.5-inch SSD to the motherboard

items.name: M.2 slot (M key)
items.answer: NVMe SSD mounted flat on the board

items.name: 24-pin ATX
items.answer: Main power from the PSU to the motherboard

items.name: PCIe 8-pin (6+2)
items.answer: Extra power to a graphics card

items.name: VGA (DE-15, blue)
items.answer: Legacy analogue video to an old monitor or projector

options: Reversible USB data, power and video
Digital video and audio to a monitor or TV
Hard disk or 2.5-inch SSD to the motherboard
NVMe SSD mounted flat on the board
Main power from the PSU to the motherboard
Extra power to a graphics card
Legacy analogue video to an old monitor or projector

hints: RJ-45 is the wider 8-wire plug on network cables; RJ-11 is the narrower phone plug.
The 24-pin block is the biggest connector in a PC; the 6+2 pin plugs into the top edge of a graphics card.
M.2 drives have no cable at all: they screw flat onto the board.

checks.label: Every connector matched to its purpose

realityNote: Shape prevents most wrong connections, but not all: a USB-C port may carry only power, or data, or video, depending on the device. Read the small symbols next to the port.
